seo.title: Best Wine Bars in Cartagena (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Uncork the best of Cartagena's wine scene! Discover top wine bars, from historic cellars to rooftop views, offering exquisite selections and perfect pairings in the Walled City.

hero.subtitle: Cartagena's burgeoning culinary scene extends to its wine offerings, with a vibrant selection of bars and restaurants providing sophisticated sips amidst historic charm and Caribbean breezes. From intimate enotecas to grand colonial settings, you'll find diverse wines to complement your tropical escape.

picks.name: El Burlador Gasterobar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Inspired by Spanish culinary traditions, El Burlador Gasterobar offers a sophisticated yet lively atmosphere with an impressive wine list focusing on Spanish and New World labels. Their expertly curated menu of tapas and larger plates perfectly complements the extensive selection, making it a favorite for both casual sips and full dining experiences. The passionate staff are always ready to guide you.
picks.whatToOrder: Enjoy a robust Rioja paired with their Gambas al Ajillo or a selection of Iberian cured meats.
picks.insiderTip: Reserve a table on the outdoor patio for excellent people-watching and a lively evening ambiance.
picks.redditQuote: "El Burlador Gasterobar has such a fantastic wine list and their tapas are seriously addictive. We went three times!"

picks.name: Carmen Cartagena
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Widely regarded as one of Cartagena's finest dining establishments, Carmen boasts an exceptional wine program designed to perfectly complement its innovative Colombian fusion cuisine. The intimate, elegant setting is perfect for a special occasion, and their knowledgeable sommelier can guide you through an extensive list of international wines, including many organic and biodynamic options. Don't miss their exquisite tasting menus with wine pairings.
picks.whatToOrder: Opt for the tasting menu with the wine pairing to experience the full breadth of their culinary and oenological expertise.
picks.insiderTip: Book well in advance, especially for weekend evenings, as it's a very popular spot.
picks.redditQuote: "The wine pairing at Carmen Cartagena was absolutely mind-blowing. Each pour elevated the dishes perfectly."

picks.name: Alma Restaurante & Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled within the luxurious Hotel Charleston Santa Teresa, Alma offers a sophisticated ambiance in a beautifully restored colonial courtyard. Their wine list is comprehensive, featuring a strong selection of South American and European labels, perfect for pairing with their refined menu of contemporary Colombian and Caribbean dishes. The live music often adds to the enchanting atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: A crisp, cool white wine (like a Sauvignon Blanc) pairs wonderfully with their signature seafood dishes, especially the Catch of the Day.
picks.insiderTip: Request a table in the open-air courtyard for the most romantic and atmospheric setting.
picks.redditQuote: "Alma's courtyard is gorgeous, and their wine list is surprisingly deep for a hotel restaurant. Great for a fancy night out."

picks.name: 1621 Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the historic convent of the Sofitel Legend Santa Clara, 1621 Restaurant offers a grand setting for a luxurious dining and wine experience. Its cellar boasts an impressive collection of international wines, particularly strong in French and Old World varietals. The elegant ambiance, impeccable service, and gourmet French-inspired cuisine make it a top choice for discerning wine lovers.
picks.whatToOrder: Explore their extensive Bordeaux or Burgundy selections to complement their exquisite steak or duck dishes.
picks.insiderTip: After dinner, enjoy a digestif or another glass of wine at El Coro Lounge Bar, also within the hotel.
picks.redditQuote: "You can't beat the setting at 1621, and their sommelier really knows their stuff. We had an incredible Chablis."

picks.name: Enoteca 1920
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As its name suggests, Enoteca 1920 is a dedicated wine bar that prides itself on its carefully curated selection of Italian and international wines. It offers a cozy, rustic-chic atmosphere perfect for a relaxed evening of wine tasting. Beyond just bottles, they also serve delicious Italian-inspired small plates and cheeses that perfectly accompany their diverse offerings.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask for their daily specials on wine by the glass, and pair it with a gourmet cheese and charcuterie board.
picks.insiderTip: This spot is great for a pre-dinner drink or a light dinner focused on wine and appetizers.
picks.redditQuote: "Enoteca 1920 is a hidden gem! Found a fantastic Sardinian Vermentino there. Definitely worth seeking out."

picks.name: La Vitrola
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An iconic Cartagena institution, La Vitrola is famed for its lively Cuban band, vibrant atmosphere, and excellent traditional Caribbean cuisine. While not strictly a wine bar, it offers a well-chosen selection of wines, particularly South American reds and crisp whites, that beautifully complement its flavorful dishes. The energy here is infectious, making for an unforgettable night.
picks.whatToOrder: Enjoy a smooth Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon with their classic local fish or Ropa Vieja.
picks.insiderTip: Reservations are essential, often weeks in advance. Dress smart casual to fit the elegant yet festive vibe.
picks.redditQuote: "La Vitrola's ambiance is legendary, and their wine list is surprisingly good for such a high-energy place. The music and food are a perfect combo."

picks.name: Mar y Zielo Cocina de Origen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mar y Zielo takes diners on a culinary journey through Colombia's diverse regions, from the mountains to the sea, with a sophisticated twist. Their wine list is thoughtfully curated to enhance these unique flavors, featuring a good range of international bottles. The elegant interior design and attentive service create a refined setting perfect for enjoying a special meal with well-chosen wine pairings.
picks.whatToOrder: A light-bodied Pinot Noir or a dry Riesling can wonderfully enhance the complex flavors of their seafood or pork dishes.
picks.insiderTip: They offer a lovely tasting menu, and the staff are excellent at recommending wines to match each course.
picks.redditQuote: "Mar y Zielo blew me away with their creative menu, and the wine recommendation from our waiter was spot-on. Such a great experience."

picks.name: Mistura
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mistura brings the vibrant flavors of Peruvian cuisine to Cartagena, with a focus on fresh seafood and a touch of Japanese (Nikkei) influence. Their extensive wine list features excellent options to complement the bold and often spicy dishes, including a strong selection of South American whites and rosés. The atmosphere is stylish and contemporary, making it a popular choice for a lively dinner.
picks.whatToOrder: Pair their renowned Cebiche Clásico with a crisp Albariño or a refreshing Torrontés.
picks.insiderTip: Try to get a table near the window overlooking the street for a blend of ambiance and people-watching.
picks.redditQuote: "You absolutely HAVE to get the ceviche at Mistura, and they have some really nice white wines that cut through the spice perfectly."

picks.name: El Santísimo
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Housed in a charming old convent, El Santísimo offers a unique 'saintly' themed dining experience with a strong emphasis on ambiance and gourmet cuisine. Their well-curated wine list features a good range of international selections, with a focus on South American and Spanish wines, designed to pair with their elegant Colombian and international dishes. It's known for its romantic and sophisticated setting.
picks.whatToOrder: A full-bodied Malbec complements their acclaimed beef tenderloin dishes perfectly.
picks.insiderTip: The restaurant is a bit tucked away; look for the entrance near the Hotel Boutique Anandá.
picks.redditQuote: "El Santísimo is so atmospheric and the food is great. Their wine selection was surprisingly good for a restaurant with such a strong theme."

picks.name: Restaurant Club de Pesca
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in a historic fort overlooking the bay, Club de Pesca offers stunning waterfront views and some of Cartagena's freshest seafood. While a classic restaurant, its wine list is comprehensive, featuring many choices that complement its coastal menu, from sparkling wines to crisp whites and lighter reds. It's an ideal spot for a leisurely meal with a beautiful sunset backdrop.
picks.whatToOrder: A refreshing bottle of Chilean Sauvignon Blanc pairs perfectly with their grilled whole fish or classic Cartagena seafood platter.
picks.insiderTip: Go just before sunset to enjoy the magnificent views of the city skyline as it lights up.
picks.redditQuote: "The views at Club de Pesca are unbeatable, and their seafood with a nice chilled white wine was pure bliss. A classic Cartagena experience."

picks.name: Alquímico
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While primarily celebrated for its incredible craft cocktails, Alquímico, housed in a magnificent colonial mansion, also offers a thoughtful selection of wines across its three distinct levels. The rooftop, in particular, provides an energetic atmosphere with great views and a curated list of approachable yet interesting wines by the glass and bottle. It's a fantastic spot for a sophisticated drink before or after dinner.
picks.whatToOrder: Choose a glass of their excellent house Malbec or Sauvignon Blanc to enjoy on the bustling rooftop.
picks.insiderTip: Arrive early (before 7 PM) to beat the crowds, especially on weekends, and snag a good spot on the rooftop.
picks.redditQuote: "Alquímico's rooftop is a must-visit. We mostly did cocktails, but their wine by the glass was surprisingly good quality for a place like that."

picks.name: Cuzco Cocina Peruana
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Cuzco offers an authentic taste of Peru, specializing in vibrant ceviches, tiraditos, and other traditional dishes. The restaurant features a well-rounded wine list with a particular strength in South American labels, which pair beautifully with the complex and fresh flavors of Peruvian cuisine. The setting is stylish and comfortable, perfect for a flavorful meal complemented by a great bottle of wine.
picks.whatToOrder: A crisp, acidic Torrontés or a dry Rosé is the ideal accompaniment to any of their fresh ceviche preparations.
picks.insiderTip: Don't miss their Pisco Sours; they are legendary and make a great start before moving on to wine.
picks.redditQuote: "Every time I'm in Cartagena, I hit up Cuzco for their ceviche. Their wine list also has some really good options to go with it."

faq.question: What is the typical price range for wine in Cartagena?
faq.answer: The price of wine in Cartagena can vary significantly. A glass of house wine at a casual spot might be COP 20,000-40,000 ($5-10 USD), while a premium glass at a fine dining restaurant could be COP 50,000-100,000+ ($12-25+ USD). Bottles typically range from COP 80,000 ($20 USD) for a decent local or South American selection to COP 400,000+ ($100+ USD) for high-end international labels.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for wine bars in Cartagena?
faq.answer: For popular or fine dining establishments like Carmen, Alma, or La Vitrola, reservations are highly recommended, especially for evening visits and weekends. For dedicated wine bars or more casual spots, you might be able to walk in, but a reservation never hurts, particularly if you have a larger group or specific seating preference.

faq.question: Are there good Colombian wines available in Cartagena?
faq.answer: Colombia is not traditionally known for its wine production due to its tropical climate. While there are a few local vineyards, their wines are generally less available and less critically acclaimed than those from neighboring South American countries like Chile and Argentina. Most wine bars in Cartagena will offer an extensive selection of international wines, particularly from South America, Spain, and Italy.

faq.question: What type of wines are most popular in Cartagena?
faq.answer: Given Cartagena's hot and humid climate, crisp white wines like Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay (often unoaked), and Albariño are very popular, especially when paired with the city's abundant seafood. Rosés are also a refreshing choice. For red wine lovers, lighter-bodied reds like Pinot Noir or full-bodied Malbecs from Argentina are frequently enjoyed, especially with meat dishes.

faq.question: Can I find natural or organic wines in Cartagena?
faq.answer: Yes, as Cartagena's culinary scene becomes more sophisticated, a growing number of establishments, particularly fine dining restaurants and specialized wine bars, are beginning to offer natural, organic, and biodynamic wine selections. It's best to inquire directly with the sommelier or staff at higher-end venues like Carmen or El Burlador Gasterobar for their current offerings.

faq.question: Are wine bars in Cartagena family-friendly?
faq.answer: Most dedicated wine bars or the bar areas of fine dining restaurants in Cartagena cater more to an adult clientele. While some restaurants, like Juan del Mar - Plaza, might be more accommodating to families during earlier hours, places like La Vitrola or Alquímico's rooftop become very lively and adult-oriented in the evenings. It's always a good idea to check with the venue if you plan to visit with children.

methodology: Our selection of Cartagena's best wine bars is based on extensive research, including expert reviews, local recommendations, and analysis of guest feedback. We prioritized venues offering diverse wine lists, knowledgeable sommeliers, appealing ambiance, and complementary food options to ensure a well-rounded and exceptional experience for every palate.
